ch7_opening.speaker: narrator
ch7_opening.text: The river is wider than any of them imagined. Brown water, moving fast in the middle, papyrus on both banks as tall as a man.

ch7_opening.speaker: aline
ch7_opening.text: We can't just walk in. Gasana can't swim. Eric can't swim. I'm not sure I can.

ch7_opening.speaker: emmanuel
ch7_opening.text: Mukamana said to cross where the water is wide and quiet. Never where it is narrow and fast.

ch7_opening.speaker: emmanuel
ch7_opening.text: Wait here, all of you. I'll find a place where we can cross.

ch7_test_north.speaker: narrator
ch7_test_north.text: Emmanuel pushes a stick into the water. It does not touch the bottom. The current pulls it from his hand. Not here.

ch7_test_mid.speaker: narrator
ch7_test_mid.text: Here the river narrows between two banks and runs fast and loud over hidden rocks. Narrow and fast. Not here.

ch7_test_ford.speaker: narrator
ch7_test_ford.text: The river spreads wide here, slow and quiet. The stick touches sand at knee depth, all the way out. Here. They can cross here.

ch7_care.speaker: narrator
ch7_care.text: Back at the camp, everyone is waiting. Gasana is shivering, his skin hot to the touch. A fever.

ch7_care.speaker: narrator
ch7_care.text: Back at the camp, everyone is waiting. Gasana is shivering, his skin hot to the touch. A fever. Joseph brought him to the storage room himself, the morning after the night everything changed.

ch7_care.speaker: aline
ch7_care.text: Innocent's bandage needs changing too. And there is so little left.

choices.text: [Food and water] Give Gasana the last food and water, so he has strength.
"We have nothing left to give him."

ch7_care.speaker: gasana
ch7_care.text: Bitter. Good. Bitter medicine works best, my mother used to say.

ch7_care.speaker: gasana
ch7_care.text: You should keep this for the young ones. But thank you.

ch7_care.speaker: gasana
ch7_care.text: Don't worry about an old man, Emmanuel. Worry about the river.

ch7_care.speaker: aline
ch7_care.text: There's one more dressing for Innocent's leg, if the medicine reaches.

ch7_care.speaker: narrator
ch7_care.text: Aline sits down heavily on the bank. Then she does not get up.

ch7_care.speaker: aline
ch7_care.text: I don't know if I can keep going.

ch7_care.speaker: emmanuel
ch7_care.text: We will go slowly. You don't have to do it alone.

ch7_care.speaker: aline
ch7_care.text: Then let's make sure no one gets left behind if we can help it.

ch7_care.speaker: aline
ch7_care.text: Take the others first. I'll go last. I'll need your shoulder.

ch7_care.speaker: narrator
ch7_care.text: Far up on the ridge behind them, there are voices. Still far away. Not for long.

ch7_aline.speaker: aline
ch7_aline.text: Take the others first. I'll be here.

ch7_wait.speaker: narrator
ch7_wait.text: They are watching the water, and the ridge.

ch7_lead_gasana.speaker: gasana
ch7_lead_gasana.text: Lead on. I will put my feet where you put yours.

ch7_lead_solange.speaker: solange
ch7_lead_solange.text: I'm ready. Don't let go of my hand in the water.

ch7_lead_claudine.speaker: claudine
ch7_lead_claudine.text: Eric, on my back. Hold on to my neck and don't look at the water.

ch7_lead_innocent.speaker: innocent
ch7_lead_innocent.text: My leg is slow, but it will get there.

ch7_aline_support.speaker: aline
ch7_aline_support.text: All right. My arm over your shoulder. Slowly.

ch7_separated.speaker: narrator
ch7_separated.text: Torches on the ridge, and then on the slope. Those still on the near bank have no time left. They run, not towards the river but along it, into the papyrus, and are gone.

ch7_separated.speaker: aline
ch7_separated.text: No. No, no, they were right there—

ch7_separated.speaker: emmanuel
ch7_separated.text: They're hiding. They know how to hide. We'll find them, Aline. When this is over, we will find them.

ch7_end.speaker: narrator
ch7_end.text: On the far bank, the group sits in the papyrus, soaked and shaking, and counts each other again.

ch7_end.speaker: narrator
ch7_end.text: They walk on into the evening, until they find people who will hide them, and then people who will feed them, and then, many days later, soldiers who tell them that the killing on this side of the river is over.
